summary: Defines MIB objects for managing interfaces that conform to Ethernet Passive Optical Networks as defined in IEEE 802.3ah-2004. It extends the existing Ethernet interface management.

eli5.summary: EPON brings Ethernet to homes through shared fiber. This lists the dials and readouts a manager can use for those fiber links.

how does an onu register with an olt
subtitle: SNMP objects for monitoring and configuring Ethernet passive optical network links, one row per virtual link.

tldr.problem: Ethernet Passive Optical Networks (EPON) add new layers to Ethernet, such as a control protocol, virtual links and forward error correction. Operators need a standard way to manage them with SNMP.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the DOT3-EPON-MIB module with four groups of objects (MPCP, OMPEmulation, FEC and an extended package) based on the IEEE 802.3ah attributes. Each virtual link gets its own interface index and its own table rows.
tldr.outcome: Managers get one standard set of counters, states and controls for EPON interfaces. Several objects are writable, so SNMP access has to be protected.

today: RFC 4837 is a Proposed Standard from July 2007. Its metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What the EPON MIB Covers
sections.content:
RFC 4837 defines a portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) for managing interfaces that follow the Ethernet Passive Optical Networks (EPON) standard in IEEE Std 802.3ah-2004. These are extended capabilities of Ethernet-like interfaces. The objects are based on the attributes in Annex 30A of that standard.

The module is written in SMIv2 and is normally accessed with the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP). It is named DOT3-EPON-MIB.
sections.eli5: It is a list of names for all the meters and switches on a fiber-to-the-home link, so any manager program can read them the same way.

sections.title: How an EPON Works
sections.content:
An EPON uses a single shared optical fiber that passive splitters divide among subscribers. The Optical Line Terminal (OLT) is the server unit at the central office. Each Optical Network Unit (ONU) is a client unit at the customer premises.

Downstream, the OLT broadcasts to all ONUs. Upstream, the ONUs share the fiber by time division multiplexing, and uplink and downlink use separate wavelengths. The Multi-Point Control Protocol (MPCP) runs in the MAC control layer. The OLT sends GATE messages that tell each ONU when to transmit and for how long, and ONUs use REPORT messages to say how much data is waiting. The scheduling algorithm that divides bandwidth is not defined in 802.3ah.

To avoid showing every ONU the traffic meant for others, the standard creates a virtual link per ONU. A Logical Link Identifier (LLID) tag in the Ethernet preamble marks the destination port downstream and the source port upstream. A further broadcast channel, tagged with an all-ones LLID, reaches all ONUs in a single copy.

New ONUs register through a handshake: the OLT sends a discovery GATE, the ONU answers with REG_REQUEST, the OLT sends REGISTER assigning the LLID, then a GATE, and the ONU replies with REGISTER_ACK. The RFC notes that higher layer protocols may be needed to authenticate the ONU. An optional forward error correction layer sits between the PCS and PMA layers and uses the code RS(239,255,8).
sections.eli5: One big fiber is shared like a school corridor. The teacher at one end (the OLT) tells each student (an ONU) when it is their turn to speak, and every student wears a name tag so messages reach the right person.

sections.title: One Interface Index per Virtual Link
sections.content:
Each EPON layer has a management interface controlled through clause 30 of 802.3ah, and the MIB follows that split into packages. At the ONU the mapping is simple: one logical and one physical interface.

At the OLT there is one physical interface plus N virtual interfaces, one for each ONU, plus one more for the broadcast virtual link. The RFC chooses to manage a virtual interface like a physical one: each virtual link gets its own ifIndex, and rows in every EPON table are indexed by it. The justification is that links differ, for example ONUs at different distances can have different bad-frame counters.

Some control objects are shared and should hold the same value for every ifIndex, but most objects differ per link. The OLT virtual interfaces do not have different physical MAC addresses, because the physical interface is the same.

Rows for the ONU, the OLT and the OLT broadcast interface are created at initialization. A row for a virtual link is created when the ONU registers and deleted when it deregisters.
sections.eli5: Every kid on the shared line gets their own mailbox number, so the manager can check each kid's mail separately even though they all share one door.

sections.title: The Four Groups of Objects
sections.content:
The module has four groups of objects.

  • MPCP (802.3ah clause 64): dot3MpcpControlTable holds configuration and status per logical link, and dot3MpcpStatTable holds statistics. The object dot3MpcpMode says whether the unit is an OLT or an ONU.
  • OMPEmulation (clause 65, point-to-point emulation): dot3OmpEmulationTable and dot3OmpEmulationStatTable, with dot3OmpEmulationType giving the unit's mode.
  • FEC: dot3EponFecTable for forward error correction configuration and status per link.
  • Extended package: dot3ExtPkgControlTable, dot3ExtPkgQueueTable, dot3ExtPkgQueueSetsTable and dot3ExtPkgOptIfTable, covering control, the ONU queues and queue sets reported in MPCP REPORT messages, and the optical interface.

The RFC includes example MPCP control table contents. For an OLT with three registered ONUs there are four rows, with link IDs 1, 2, 3 and 65535 for the broadcast link. An unregistered ONU shows dot3MpcpRegistrationState as unregistered and a link ID of 0.
sections.eli5: The meters are sorted into four drawers: one for the turn-taking rules, one for the name tags, one for the error-fixing helper, and one for extras like the light-power meter.

sections.title: Relation to Other MIB Modules
sections.content:
The EPON MIB does not repeat objects that other modules already define. Implementing it MUST include the Interfaces MIB (RFC 2863), the Ethernet-like Interfaces MIB (RFC 3635) and the MAU MIB (RFC 4836). For example, the document defines dot3MpcpRemoteMACAddress only, because the local MAC address is already in the Ethernet-like MIB.

The OLT physical interface is the lower layer of the virtual link interfaces in the ifStack and ifInvStack tables. In the examples the interfaces report ethernetCsmacd (6), an MTU of 1522 and a speed of 1000000000.

The EFM OAM MIB (RFC 4878) MAY be implemented alongside, with one instance per LLID. The Bridge MIB modules MAY be implemented on an OLT, where each LLID maps to a bridge port. The broadcast virtual interface has no bridge port.
sections.eli5: This new list does not copy meters that already exist elsewhere. It just says which older lists you must also have.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Several objects are read-write or read-create, and changing them can disrupt service. The RFC lists examples: dot3MpcpAdminState can disable MPCP, dot3EponFecMode and dot3ExtPkgObjectFecEnabled can turn off forward error correction and degrade the optical link, and dot3ExtPkgObjectReset and dot3ExtPkgObjectPowerDown can reset or power down the interface. Other objects change registration, report thresholds, optical power thresholds or optical transmission.

Readable objects can also be sensitive because they reveal performance and configuration. The RFC recommends SNMPv3 with cryptographic authentication and privacy, and says deploying SNMP versions before SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: Some of the dials can switch the whole fiber off, so only trusted people should be allowed to turn them, and the messages to the dials should be locked.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: IANA allocated a single object identifier for the MODULE-IDENTITY of the DOT3-EPON-MIB module under the MIB-2 tree. The descriptor dot3EponMIB is assigned { mib-2 155 } in the SMI Numbers registry.
sections.eli5: The module got an official number in the big phone book of managed things, so nobody else uses it.
